result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks, signalized crossings, and marked zebra crosswalks. However, the crosswalk markings are significantly faded and the presence of parked cars near the intersection may create sightline issues.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The zebra-style crosswalk markings are heavily worn, reducing their visibility to approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the right side of the street are positioned close to the crossing, potentially obscuring pedestrians from the view of oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street, adjacent to the sidewalk

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: Cracking and wear in the asphalt within the crossing area could present a minor tripping hazard.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway surface within the crosswalk area

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Refresh
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk with high-visibility thermoplastic markings to ensure it is clearly visible to motorists.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking within 20-30 feet of the crosswalk to improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position before they enter the roadway.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility continental crosswalk markings and a bollard-protected curb extension on the left side to improve pedestrian visibility and reduce crossing distance. While sidewalks are in good condition and street lighting is present, the lack of visible pedestrian-specific signals and potential sightline obstructions from parked vehicles on the right side are notable deficiencies.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the right side of the street near the crosswalk may block the sightlines between drivers and pedestrians entering the crossing.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway, upstream of the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signalization
hazards.description: No pedestrian-specific signal heads are visible at this signalized intersection, which can lead to confusion about when it is safe to cross.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk on the right side, potentially using bollards or planters, to improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Signal Installation
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers and implement a Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI) to give pedestrians a head start.

interventions.title: Raised Crosswalk
interventions.description: Elevate the crosswalk to the level of the sidewalk to act as a speed table and further increase pedestrian visibility.

result.summary: The image depicts an urban intersection with basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks, curb ramps, and signalized crossings. However, the crosswalk markings are significantly faded and the roadway surface within the crossing area is uneven due to patching.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The transverse crosswalk lines are worn and lack high visibility, potentially reducing driver awareness of the crossing zone.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Degraded Road Surface
hazards.description: Uneven asphalt and patches within the crosswalk area create potential tripping hazards for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway surface within the marked crossing

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Replace faded transverse lines with continental or ladder-style markings to increase visibility to motorists.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and improve sight lines between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The street features high-visibility continental crosswalk markings and wide, well-maintained sidewalks with street trees. However, the crossing distance is significant due to a wide painted buffer area, and there is a lack of physical refuge or active traffic control devices.

hazards.name: Wide crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians are exposed to traffic for a long duration while crossing multiple lanes and a wide painted buffer without a physical refuge.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway at the crosswalk

hazards.name: Uncontrolled crossing
hazards.description: There are no visible signals or signs requiring drivers to stop or yield at this high-visibility crossing.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised concrete island in the center painted buffer to provide a safe mid-point for pedestrians and reduce exposure time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking/buffer lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB)
interventions.description: Install pedestrian-activated flashing lights to increase driver yielding rates at this uncontrolled crossing.
